hypothesis: Measurement (bot skill): the gap comes from how the bots play, not from the design. The scripted lines and Hard adapters skip key buys, place badly for Rings and Nests, don't thank Shy units or tithe, or switch lines badly. If that's true, a skilled player with the same shops would get close to the paper boards, and whenever the key pieces are on the board, the board would grow at the rate the cards say.
expected_if_true:
- Bots buy far fewer key pieces than the shops offer.
- Annis, Fetch, the B1 stander or the Lump stand in the wrong slots.
- Many Rings sit under Shy units or on empty slots.
- Lob and Silky stay on the board and are never thanked.
- Cluricaun tier-ups miss the rainbow by only 1–2 slots, so a human could fix them.
- Homecomings don't come back doubled, or the carry never flies.
- Seats that do have the key pieces still end far below the paper because of misplays.
- The tempo line's switch at R7 drags its boards down.
would_rule_out:
- Bots buy key pieces at close to the rate shops offer them.
- Placements match the line files.
- Each engine card does what its text says whenever it is on the board.
- Seats that have the pieces land near the matching paper row.
- Missed Cluricaun tier-ups are mostly 3 or more slots short, so a human couldn't have finished the rainbow either.
- Real shops almost never offer the paper's arrivals on the paper's rounds.

**7. Real bot leaks I found.**
- **Most of the line files' instructions are never carried out.** `normalize_wave1` keeps only tribe, priority, keep, climb, the engine flag, the switch and fly_policy. `buy_only_if`, `place`, `thank`, `save`, `spells`, `max_copies`, `stayer_cap`, `golden_egg` and `harvest_supper_rounds` are stored in `source_policy`, which no code reads. `bot_pass3.gd` hard-codes the main Fairy actions instead.
- **Birds keep extra stayers.** At R12, 58% of boards have a duplicated stayer, and 50% have more than the line's cap of 4 stayers.
- **The Birds carry stays home.** From R7 on, on turns when a Bird flew and an eligible bigger flier was home, that bigger flier stayed home 1,423 times and flew 200 times (88% stayed). The guard is on for 36% of seats at R10 and 63% at R12. The paper models no health, so it never pays this cost.
- **Fairy boards have empty slots.** At R12 a Ring board has 1.2 empty slots on average, and a Court board 1.4–1.9 when the Queen is down; one empty slot is the Queen's designed tithe slot. Filling each empty slot with a median body from the same board would add 17–18% (median).
- **Lob is thanked at 3 turns whether or not Silky is on the board.** The line says to wait for 6 turns without Silky.
- **Hob is sold rather than thanked:** 140 of 250 departures, including 21 while Silky was on the board, where a thank would have grown Ring size.
- **Line seats place blind and by rule.** `line_brain.gd` sets `PLACE_BLIND`, so there is no scouting and no placement search. Jack Daw, the Whistlers, the Changeling and Witch stander rules, and Horseshoe aim at nothing in particular.
- **The tempo switch is not the problem.** Tempo seats reach 0.72× of their paper at R12, and both Birds lines finish around 265.

hypothesis: SYSTEM / SUPPLY. The shop delivers Birds and Fairies engine pieces too rarely and too late for the paper's fixed arrival rounds. In this run's pool there are 6 tribes of 16 cards plus 13 neutrals, so 21 cards share each of T1-T3 (20 at T4, 13 at T5-T6). Draws pick a tier by odds, then a copy at random within that tier, so one shop slot shows a given card only (tier odds)/21. A committed seat gets about 1 to 2.5 fills a round. The paper plans assume Annis R3, Cluricaun and Lob R5, Redbreast and Jay R3, Stork R7, and so on, every game. So the real lines reach their engines late or never. On top of that, other seats in the shared pool take the copies.
level: system (supply); also measurement (the paper's arrival assumption)
expected_if_true: (1) At the paper's arrival rounds, the chance a seat has even seen the key card is far below 100%. (2) Seats own about what they see: bots buy on sight, so supply is the binding limit, not the policy. (3) Seats that did get the engine pieces early land near paper at R12, and giving every seat the pieces would close most of the gap. (4) Depletion by other seats on the same tribe lowers offer rates noticeably.
would_rule_out: Any of these would rule it out: offer odds near 100% by the paper rounds; ownership well below offer rates (a policy problem); seats that hold the engine early still far below paper (the engine under-produces, not under-arrives); or a stat gap that doesn't change when the pieces are present.

hypothesis: JOURNEY and ROLE (keystone dependence). Each wave 1 engine hangs on one or two named keystone cards. For Fairies these are Old Moth Annis for Ring count, then Cluricaun, Lob and Silky followed by the Monarch for Ring size, and the Queen for the Court. For Birds they are the early T1 flier that becomes the carry, plus Mrs Stork and Mother Goose. Real shops deliver each keystone far less often than the paper's 100%. Without it a committed board stays near flat, so the line's R12 median is set by games missing the keystone. Boards that have it should sit near paper.
expected_if_true: (a) At least 40% of committed games lack each keystone by R12. (b) Boards with the keystone reach a median R12 of 0.7x paper or more (inside the 0.5-2x band). (c) Boards without it grow at about x1.1 a round or less over R8-R12 within each seat. (d) Dropping the keystone-missing games closes most of the log gap to paper. (e) The cards themselves do their job once on the board.
would_rule_out: Any of these would rule it out: boards with the keystone still far below 0.5x paper; boards without it growing almost as fast as boards with it; a small with/without gap; or keystones that are present but don't deliver their effect (that is a role failure, not a supply failure).

hypothesis: Distribution (09d lens): committed wave-1 games split in two. A minority assemble the engine (Birds: Stork + Cuckoo/Lump/Goose cycling; Fairies: Ring size from Cluricaun/Lob/Silky/Monarch on Annis-fed Rings) and go big, while the rest stay flat. The median sits in the flat group, so the median-to-paper gap measures how often the engine assembles, not how strong it is. If so, raising dials (h, Cuckoo share, Monarch, Ring growth) would mainly stretch the top and widen the spread instead of lifting the typical game.
level: Distribution of R12/R14 pre-start boards across committed games, and inside each board (09d). Overlaps the Journey and System levels through engine assembly.
expected_if_true: (1) Each line's log-board distribution at R12/R14 is bimodal: two KDE modes, Sarle BC > 0.555, and a 2-Gaussian mixture clearly beats one, with the upper part about 10-40% of games. (2) Each game's growth rate is bimodal too: a group compounding at about x1.5 a round and a group at about x1.1-1.2. (3) A wide tail: at least 15-25% of boards at 2x the line median, at or above Battlegrounds' 23% at turn 12. (4) A step, not a slope, against engine presence. Engine-assembled games are at least 2x the others, and they reach roughly the paper figure (0.5-2x paper). (5) Re-pricing boards with a growth dial raises p90 a lot and the median little.
would_rule_out: Unimodal log distributions in every committed line. Unimodal growth rates per game. A share at 2x median at or below Battlegrounds' reference. Stats rising smoothly with engine throughput instead of stepping. Engine-assembled games still far below paper. Any one of these rules out the 'split' form. If the assembled games also miss paper, the engine's output per piece (the ceiling) is short as well as the floor.
evidence:
Scripts (python3 -I, read-only on captures; NO Godot), in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-alex-code-Bramble-ideation/5369878e-e379-478d-ac97-3201f49297d2/scratchpad/triage-w1/: load.py (all 32 chunk boards + players + seat labels -> boards.pkl; 30,626 boards, 0 line/start-line mismatches), dist.py, keystone.py, growth.py, counterfactual.py, ringsize.py; outputs in *.out.txt beside them. Medians match the accounting (270 / 260.5 / 142 / 160 at R12).

NO SPLIT. Committed lines at R8-R14: Sarle BC on log stats 0.25-0.42, under the 0.555 bimodality line everywhere. The KDE finds one mode in every line and round. A 2-Gaussian mixture is not preferred for Birds (dBIC -19 to +11, up to +33 at tempo R14). For Fairies it only splits off a 2-10% upper tail at R9-R11 (dBIC 21-46). Positive control: the mixed-tribe Hard field does split (dBIC 334-618 at R10-R13), so the test can see a split. Growth per game from R8 to R14 has one peak too (BC 0.39-0.46), median x1.36 / 1.35 / 1.23 / 1.32 (homecoming / tempo / ring / court). Only 21% / 15% / 6% / 17% of seats compound at x1.5 or more.

TAIL AT OR BELOW BATTLEGROUNDS. Boards at 2x their line's R12 median: homecoming 12.3%, tempo 10.9%, ring 7.3%, court 10.8% (about ±3pp), against Battlegrounds' 23% at turn 12. At R14: 15.6 / 16.3 / 16.8 / 22.5% against 23%. Pooled all 8 seats: R8 1.2%, R10 6.7%, R12 15.7%, R14 20.7% against Battlegrounds' 13-14% from turn 8. So Bramble's spread opens about 3 rounds late and is never wider. p90/p50 at R12 is 1.84-2.12 (Battlegrounds 2.53). Even the best games miss paper. Fairies p99 at R12 is 0.88x paper for ring and 0.61x for court; 0.6% and 0.0% of games reach paper. Homecoming p90 is 0.93x. Biggest unit's share at R12 is 36% for Birds and 29-32% for Fairies, against Battlegrounds' 34%. The Fairy carry line's intended 45% is not forming.

ENGINE LINK IS A SLOPE, NOT A STEP. Birds: R12 board against homecomings over R8-R12, Spearman 0.59-0.64. Medians: 183 at 0-2 homecomings (29% of games, 0.30x paper), 273 at 3-4, 336 at 5-6, 383 at 7-8, 547 at 9-11 (5.6%, 0.89x). The paper assumes 10; the real median is 4 (p90 8). 35-50% of captured rounds have no homecoming. Counting engine pieces is a weak predictor (rho 0.24); 4-5 of 6 pieces gives a median of only 0.51x paper. Tempo seats with 7-8 homecomings already reach 0.99x paper. Fairies: board against Ring size x Rings, rho 0.82-0.93. Ring size at R12 has a median of 2 (p90 4); 29-36% of games are still at size 1, and about 66% at R10. Games at size 6 or more (6-9%) reach 286 (ring, 0.54x) and 470 (court, 0.50x). Even the assembled Fairy engine is at half of paper: the court has 23 Rings on occupied slots against paper's 76 in total. Cluricaun does nothing: median Ring size 2.0 with it and 2.0 without; size 4+ is 19.0% with it and 18.7% without. Lob and Silky are seldom owned (14% and 7%). Monarch is in 88-91% of the 2x boards. Reaching tier 6 early has no link for Birds (T6 by R9 gives 220, below 296 for T6 at R12). It has a positive link for Fairies: T6 by R9 gives 186/206 against 133/146.

SNOWBALL IS IN LEVEL, NOT RATE. Of seats in the top 10% at R10, 48-58% are still top 10% at R14 (court 27%). Of seats in the bottom half at R10, 2-4% get there. Rank correlation between the R8 level and later growth is -0.19 to +0.18.

STATIC RE-PRICING (Fairies R12; no re-simulation of fights or gold; direction only). Doubling Ring growth (a ceiling dial) raises the median 1.18x / 1.15x, p90 from 261 to 373 and 327 to 480, and the 2x-median share from 7.3 to 12.8% and 10.8 to 19.1%. At R14 the court's p10/p50 falls from 0.44 to 0.30. Starting Ring size +2 (a floor lever) raises the median 1.48x / 1.62x, keeps p90/p50 flat at 1.80 / 1.87, and leaves the 2x share at 6.6 / 7.3%. Giving every game size 6 or more lifts the median to 0.51x / 0.37x paper.
share_of_gap:
The split in the hypothesis explains 0% of the gap in every line, because no line shows a split. The corollary holds and does explain much of it: the typical game runs a partial engine, and dials mostly stretch the top. Measured as a share of the R12 log-gap closed when a game reaches paper throughput (an upper bound, since those games are also luckier on gold and survival):
- birds_homecoming: up to about 85%. Games with 9-11 homecomings reach 0.89x paper, against a 0.44x median, so the dials work once the engine cycles; its cycling rate is the gap.
- birds_tempo: about 100%. 7-8 homecomings already gives 0.99x.
- fairies_ring: about 50%. Ring size 6 gives 0.51-0.54x, against 0.27x.
- fairies_court: about 45-60%. Size 6 gives 0.37x (static) to 0.50x (observed), against 0.17x.
For Fairies, the rest is the Ring count on occupied slots (median 16-23) and the paper's guaranteed arrivals and sequences. That part is outside this lens.
